players.product: antibody discovery and multispecific T-cell engager platform

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Carl Hansen on what the ABCL635 Phase II data settled: whether NK3R in the preoptic nucleus matters, the risk he had flagged before the readout, is now 'completely unimportant' ('It is all about the KNDy neurons'). With a frequency reduction well over the approval bar, Phase III enrollment can keep a baseline of about 10 events per day, and the Phase II would have been adequately powered with 15 patients in each arm. He does not think a direct head-to-head trial against the small molecules is needed to convince patients or caregivers; it may have value in pricing discussions and could be run as a side study after the registrational trials. He thinks the efficacy is 'highly unlikely to miss' in Phase III ('we are very bullish on that'). At 12 weeks he expects efficacy to wane as the drug washes out, by design, and said the effect is probably lasting longer than some biomarker data would have suggested.
quarterly_data.figure: baseline about 10 events per day; 15 patients in each arm would have sufficed
